headline: Supertanker Carrying More Than Two Million Barrels of Oil Sinks in Persian Gulf, Tehran Says - World - News - pravda.sk
summary: A supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of oil sank in the Persian Gulf after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz and catching fire, according to Tehran.
why: The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important oil transit chokepoints, so disruptions there can affect global crude supply and freight costs.
why_moved: The sinking follows a mine strike and fire in the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil route, which raises concerns about crude supply disruption.
